I found nothing to flag. Every claim in the document is backed by the record, and the document has no went_wrong field to check for misplaced items.

- **Root cause:** This was the closest call. The document states it flatly, while the record treats the flag change as a suspected cause. I let it stand because the logs line up closely with the flag change. The division-by-zero errors at `spend_summary.py:47` start in the same minute the flag was switched on (11:40). They don't appear anywhere in the 30 minutes of logs before that. They continue through every minute the flag stayed on.
- **Third contributing factor (no paging):** The record only says no on-call incident was linked. The document goes a little further and says the alert itself was not wired to paging. I counted that as a fair paraphrase rather than a new fact.
- **Not judged:** The action items and the "had it been otherwise" what-ifs.

supported.quote: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests through the spend-summary code, which divided by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and failed the request with a ZeroDivisionError.
The record does not show why the divisor was zero on these requests.
Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero, so those pages failed.
If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again, account page requests could fail again with the same division by zero.
Shoppers' account page requests failed, well above the usual low level of failures.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were logged over {G5309.3} and were not seen in the log window before the onset.

The spend-summary code ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations were split between off and on in {G971b.6} and were all on over {Gce95.4}. Before that, the flag was off over {G7e5d.4}.
The ClientDisconnected account page errors: they were already logged before the onset, over {G46bc.3}, while account pages otherwise rendered normally.
The flag change broke account pages because the spend-summary path it turned on divides by a value that was zero on these requests.
The flag change reached all account page traffic in a single step. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on a rising error rate were seen for monthly-spend-feature.
No test or pre-production check of the spend-summary path was seen before the flag was switched on in production.
The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to on-call paging, so nobody was paged when it fired.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
